# halos_service_token (Resource)

A halo-server service-account token (ADR-0036): one role, optionally bounded to rings and units (ADR-0037), for automation.

Every argument forces a new token, because a token cannot be edited; destroying the resource revokes it.

~> **The secret is stored in Terraform state.** `token` is returned by halo-server exactly once, at create, and Terraform has to keep it to be useful. Use an encrypted remote backend (or OpenTofu state encryption) and restrict who can read state. Marking it sensitive only hides it from CLI output. An imported token has no `token` value: the secret cannot be read back.

~> **Creating needs an interactive session.** halo-server only lets a signed-in human create tokens (a token cannot mint its successor), so the provider needs `session` (or `HALO_SESSION`) for create. Refresh, import and destroy work with a service token.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A read-only token for a dashboard, valid for 30 days and limited to one ring.
resource "halos_service_token" "dashboard" {
  name        = "fleet-dashboard"
  role        = "viewer"
  ttl         = "720h"
  owner       = "platform"
  description = "Grafana datasource for the canary ring"

  scope = {
    rings = ["ring1-canary"]
  }
}

# The secret exists only in state: send it straight to a secret manager and
# keep state encrypted.
output "dashboard_token" {
  value     = halos_service_token.dashboard.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Lowercase name (a-z, 0-9, `.`, `_`, `-`; at most 63 characters). Shown in the audit log as `service-account:<name>:<id>`. Changing it forces a new token.
- `role` (String) One of viewer, operator, approver, auditor, admin. May not exceed the creator's own permissions. Changing it forces a new token.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description. Changing it forces a new token.
- `owner` (String) Free-text owner, for example a team name. Changing it forces a new token.
- `scope` (Attributes) Bounds the role to rings and units that exist in policy and lie within the creator's admin grants. Omit for a global token. Must name at least one ring or unit. Changing it forces a new token. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope))
- `ttl` (String) Lifetime as a duration such as `720h`: at least `1h`, at most halo-server's `--service-token-max-ttl` (default and maximum 90 days). Omit for the server default. Changing it forces a new token. After import the value is derived from the token's dates and is whole hours, minutes or seconds (`720h`, `90m`).

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time, RFC 3339.
- `created_by` (String) The admin who created the token.
- `expires_at` (String) Expiry time, RFC 3339. An expired token stays in state until it is destroyed or revoked.
- `id` (String) The token id (16 hex characters). Also the import id.
- `principal` (String) The audit identity, `service-account:<name>:<id>`.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The secret (`halo_sat_...`), for use as `Authorization: Bearer`. Available only at create and stored in state, so use encrypted state; null after import.

<a id="nestedatt--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scope`

Optional:

- `rings` (Set of String) Ring names.
- `units` (Set of String) Unit names.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by token id (the 16 hex characters from `halo service-token list`).
# The secret cannot be recovered: `token` stays null.
terraform import halos_service_token.dashboard 0123456789abcdef
```
